literal: a shining or appearing forth; prati- + √bhās 'to shine' + ghañ

derivations.affix: ghañ; verse 83 then adds mayat and feminine ṅīp in pratibhāsa-mayī
derivations.qualification: The completed noun carries the contextual range appearance/presentation. The root and affix do not by themselves establish that the appearance is false.

definition_claims.text: *Pratibhāsa* is a shining or appearing forth. In verse 83, *pratibhāsa-mayī* qualifies a *jīva-śakti*: the power is said to consist in *pratibhāsa*.

The suffix *mayat* in *pratibhāsa-mayī* expresses composition or prevalence: the feminine power is made of, or pervaded by, manifest appearance. The verse then says that this power attained a threefold flashing-forth.
This passage-specific entry does not equate *pratibhāsa* with the later technical adjective *prātibhāsika*. It also keeps verse 83's *pratibhāsa* distinct from verse 81's *pratibhā*.

exposition_sections.title: Appearance as the composition of a power

claims.text: The Dhātupāṭha gives √bhās, *dīptau*, 'in shining.' The formation prati-√bhās + ghañ yields a noun of shining or appearing forth; verse 83 adds *mayat* to say that the *jīva-śakti* consists in it.
The verse describes the power's constitution and threefold manifestation. Whether that manifest appearance should receive a further ontological label is not settled by the lexical formation alone.

invariant_definition: In this reader, *pratibhāsa* is a shining or appearing forth. Verse 83 uses *pratibhāsa-mayī* of a *jīva-śakti*, stating that the power consists in manifest appearance. The word does not, by formation alone, mean illusion or falsity.

per_school.definition: A *jīva-śakti* belonging to the supreme self is described as *pratibhāsa-mayī*, consisting in manifest appearance, and as attaining a threefold flashing-forth.

translator_note: 'Appearance' is serviceable only if it is not made to imply unreality automatically. 'Shining-forth' preserves √bhās; 'manifest appearance' fits the local *-mayī* construction.
